note: Dimension matrix for the framework-gap argument only (spine lines 1-2 / story-graph GAP N04). Benchmark and baseline sources (SRC-011 through SRC-030) are evidentiary comparators for the Results section, not part of the gap argument, and are not repeated here; see claims/claim_evidence_map.json and evidence/research_evidence.json for their role.
dimensions_chosen: method family (what the framework is built around)
capability coverage (which of the 5 pieces it supplies)
domain scope (general-purpose vs. one task family)

matrix.problem_framing: compose LLM calls and tools into chains/graphs
matrix.key_assumption: the hard part is composing calls, not executing arbitrary code safely
matrix.data_eval: none (a library, not a benchmarked system)
matrix.weakness_limit: only 'basic runtime support' per the citing paper -- no built-in sandbox, browser, or evaluation harness
matrix.relation_to_us: OpenHands remains compatible with tool-calling agents built this way (E006), but adds the sandboxed execution and evaluation layers this dimension lacks

matrix.key_assumption: agents coordinate mainly through natural-language messages
matrix.data_eval: none reported in the citing paper
matrix.strength: adds real Python/bash execution beyond pure chat frameworks
matrix.weakness_limit: execution is stateless (no persistent sandboxed session)
matrix.relation_to_us: OpenHands' actions execute inside one persistent, stateful Docker sandbox per session (E009)

matrix.key_assumption: role specialization plus a light code-execution tool is enough
matrix.data_eval: none reported in the citing paper
matrix.weakness_limit: code-interpreter feature is 'limited' per the citing paper
matrix.relation_to_us: OpenHands exposes the full agent action space (bash + IPython + browser) rather than one constrained interpreter tool

matrix.key_assumption: the browser is the whole environment
matrix.strength: clean, reusable browsing primitives, adopted directly by OpenHands
matrix.weakness_limit: covers browsing only; no code-execution sandbox, tool library, or delegation
matrix.relation_to_us: OpenHands adopts BrowserGym's action primitives (E004, E011) for one of its three action types, adding the rest of the platform around it

matrix.key_assumption: the main lever for better agent behavior is prompt/pipeline optimization
matrix.data_eval: none reported in the citing paper
matrix.weakness_limit: not an execution environment; no sandbox, browser, or evaluation harness
matrix.relation_to_us: orthogonal: OpenHands could in principle host a DSPy-optimized agent, but supplies the runtime DSPy itself does not

matrix.key_assumption: encoding standard operating procedures improves multi-agent software work
matrix.data_eval: software-generation case studies (not in the 15-benchmark suite compared here)
matrix.strength: structured role/procedure design for team-like agent collaboration
matrix.weakness_limit: focused on the software-team process pattern, not a general execution/evaluation platform
matrix.relation_to_us: OpenHands' AgentDelegateAction (E016) covers one general delegation mechanism rather than a fixed team procedure

matrix.problem_framing: represent and optimize multi-agent systems as graphs
matrix.key_assumption: agent systems are well modeled as graphs of operations/edges that can be optimized automatically
matrix.weakness_limit: OpenHands' own authors note their platform's workflow is still largely handcrafted, unlike GPTSwarm's optimizable graphs (E184)
matrix.relation_to_us: integrated directly as one AgentHub agent (E019) and named as a candidate future direction for automatic workflow generation (E184, N30)

matrix.source: SRC-008/009/010 (Yang et al. 2024 SWE-Agent; Zhang et al. 2024b AutoCodeRover; Xia et al. 2024 Agentless)
matrix.key_assumption: a carefully crafted, task-specific agent-computer interface (or search+edit pipeline) is the main lever for this one task
matrix.strength: strong, purpose-built performance on GitHub-issue resolution specifically
matrix.weakness_limit: scoped to one task family; not evaluated as general-purpose agents across browsing or other assistance tasks
matrix.relation_to_us: OpenHands' unmodified generalist CodeActAgent reaches 22.0-26.0% on the same benchmark (E051) while also running on 14 other, non-SWE benchmarks
